description: Sotto Core: a local web app (Node server on 127.0.0.1 + React UI) that listens to a group brainstorm via Meta Muse Voice Transcribe (realtime, DIARIZATION), keeps a living board, and contributes to the group only when it matters: scored, pause-timed, rate-limited interjections (contradiction, factual error, untested assumption, dropped thread), measured by an eval harness against fixtures with planted moments. Also answers when addressed by wake word, using Muse Spark 1.3 with web search and sandboxed HTML artifacts. Every session saves to a folder. Full spec: tasks/prd-sotto-core.md

userStories.title: Fixture generator, script schema, and conversation fixtures (PRD US-002 part 1)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need recorded two-speaker conversations generated from scripts so features can be tested without people talking into a mic.
acceptanceCriteria: Zod schema in shared/fixtures.ts for fixtures/scripts/<name>.json: { lines: [{ speaker: 'A'|'B', text, pauseAfterMs }], wakeQuestions: [{ line, question }], moments: [{ id, type: 'contradiction'|'factual_error'|'untested_assumption'|'dropped_thread', setupLines: number[], triggerLine, deadlineLine, expectedLevel: 'glow'|'interject', description }] } (line numbers are 0-based indexes into lines)

fixtures/make_fixture.py turns a script into fixtures/audio/<name>.wav (mono, 16-bit PCM, 24 kHz) using Chatterbox TTS run with ~/Developer/Chatterbox/venv/bin/python; speaker A uses ~/Developer/Chatterbox/voices/maddie.pt, speaker B uses Chatterbox's default voice; lines joined with their pauses
make_fixture.py also writes fixtures/audio/<name>.timing.json with startMs and endMs for every line
fixtures/README.md documents usage: ~/Developer/Chatterbox/venv/bin/python fixtures/make_fixture.py fixtures/scripts/<name>.json

npm run fixtures:check validates every script against the schema, checks setupLines < triggerLine <= deadlineLine and all line indexes exist, and checks each script has a matching .wav and .timing.json

Fixtures created, scripted, generated and committed: brainstorm (1–3 min, two speakers planning a product; at least 5 points, 1 decision, 1 open question; no moments, no wake phrase), ask-search (~45 s; includes 'Sotto, what do the main competitors charge per month?'), ask-diagram (~45 s; includes 'Sotto, can you sketch the user flow we just described as a diagram?'), no-wake (~45 s; includes 'so to speak', 'Soto's restaurant', 'sotto voce'; no wake phrase, no moments)
npm run fixtures:check passes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Done. All 8 criteria met; npm run fixtures:check, typecheck and test pass. Rendered durations: brainstorm 120.1s, ask-search 48.5s, ask-diagram 42.0s, no-wake 45.0s. Chatterbox runs ~2.5x real time on --device mps (24-line brainstorm took ~13 min wall clock), so budget time when generating the US-003 moment fixtures. The moment-* fixtures named in the PRD table are US-003, not this story.

userStories.title: Planted-moment fixtures (PRD US-002 part 2)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need conversations containing planted moments Sotto should catch, so the interjection engine can be measured.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixtures scripted with annotated moments, generated and committed (each 1–3 min, two speakers planning a product, natural-sounding with some filler and back-and-forth):
moment-contradiction: a budget or deadline constraint stated early (setupLines), contradicted later (triggerLine); expectedLevel interject
moment-fact: a confidently stated, checkably wrong fact (e.g. a wrong product launch year or market size); expectedLevel interject
moment-assumption: the plan rests on an assumption nobody questions (e.g. 'users will obviously pay monthly'); expectedLevel glow
moment-dropped: a promising idea raised, interrupted, never returned to; later the discussion reaches a point where it applies; expectedLevel glow
moment-mixed: ~3 minutes, two moments of different types, with long stretches where nothing should be said
Each moment's description explains the setup and trigger in one or two sentences
npm run fixtures:check passes
Typecheck passes

Durations 104.3s/112.8s/121.9s/127.8s and moment-mixed 194.7s with quiet stretches of 67s, 43s and 30s around its two moments. Four of the five WAVs were already rendered by a cut-off iteration; this one only had to render moment-mixed (809s wall clock, 4.15x real time).

userStories.title: AudioSource interface and WAV replay (PRD US-003 part 1)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to stream a fixture WAV through the same audio interface the mic will use.
acceptanceCriteria: server/audio/AudioSource.ts defines an interface emitting PCM16 mono 24 kHz chunks of 80 ms (3,840 bytes) plus an end signal
WavReplaySource reads a WAV from fixtures/audio/ and emits chunks paced at real time with a drift-corrected timer (not bare setInterval)
WavReplaySource rejects WAVs that are not mono 16-bit 24 kHz with a clear error
Unit test: replaying a 2.0 s WAV emits 25 chunks over 1.9–2.2 s
Unit test: average chunk interval over a 10 s WAV is 80 ms ± 10 ms
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Done; all 7 criteria met (npm run typecheck, npm test: 29 tests, npm run fixtures:check). AudioSource/AudioSink interfaces + chunk constants in server/audio/AudioSource.ts (AUDIO_CHUNK_BYTES=3840, AUDIO_CHUNK_MS=80, AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE=24000); onEnd(reason) is the end signal ('complete' | 'stopped'). WavReplaySource validates format in its constructor and paces with a drift-corrected timer (delay measured from stream start, catch-up on a late tick); measured 25 chunks in 2001 ms for a 2.0 s WAV and avg interval 80.02 ms over 10 s. Introduced server/clock.ts (Clock = now() + setTimeout -> cancel, systemClock on performance.now()) because the project convention forbids Date.now(); US-006 should extend this file rather than add a second clock. The RIFF reader now lives in server/audio/wav.ts and scripts/check-fixtures.ts imports it. No UI work here: the source selector and Start/Stop from PRD US-003 belong to US-012.

userStories.title: Realtime transcription client and event capture (PRD US-004)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need recorded event streams from Meta's realtime transcription so the parser is built against what the API actually sends.
acceptanceCriteria: server/asr/realtimeClient.ts opens wss://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/realtime and sends the JSON handshake as the first frame within 10 s: authorization.accessToken 'Bearer <key>', audioEncoding 'PCM_24KHZ', model 'muse-voice-transcribe-1.0', mode 'DIARIZATION', keywords ['Sotto'] (see https://dev.meta.ai/docs/speech-to-text and https://dev.meta.ai/docs/api-reference/voice/realtime)
Streams binary chunks from an AudioSource, sends {"type":"endStream"} at end of input, and reads until the server closes with code 1000
Close codes: 1000 done; 1008 logged as fatal config/pacing error; 1011 and 1013 retried with backoff 1 s, 2 s, 4 s (max 3 tries)
Every server frame is appended with receive time (ms since stream start) to a JSONL file
npm run capture -- <fixture> replays fixtures/audio/<fixture>.wav and writes fixtures/events/<fixture>.jsonl; npm run capture -- --all does every fixture
Captured event files for all fixtures are committed

fixtures/events/NOTES.md documents the actual event shapes seen (speechStart, transcript partials, speechEnd, speechComplete, speaker), how speaker events relate to turns and partials, and how 'Sotto' was spelled in transcripts
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Done; all 8 criteria met (npm run typecheck, npm test: 35 tests, npm run fixtures:check: 9 fixtures OK). RealtimeTranscriptionClient is the AudioSink: it queues chunks and flushes whenever a socket is open, so audio produced during a retry backoff is held and sent on the new session (unit-tested against a local WebSocketServer, no network). Close handling: 1000 done, 1008 fatal, 1011/1013 retried 1s/2s/4s (max 3). All nine captures are committed; a cut-off previous iteration had left moment-dropped truncated at 111.6s of 127.8s and moment-mixed at 13s of 194.7s, and no-wake missing, so those three were re-captured. fixtures:check now catches that case (capture must end with the post-endStream final:true frame and audioProcessedMs must reach the WAV's end). NOTES.md is written from the real captures: 198 turns, all with frame order speechStart -> partials -> speaker -> speechEnd -> speechComplete, exactly one speaker frame per turn, no turnId on transcript/speaker frames, 601-762 ms processing lag. Two findings the next stories need: (1) brainstorm's longest visible silence is 1,084 ms, so US-006's 'pause >= 1.5 s in brainstorm' criterion cannot pass on the current audio - NOTES.md has the fix; (2) ask-search's wake line transcribes WITHOUT the scripted comma or question mark (' Sotto what do the main competitors charge per month. '), so US-024 must not require that punctuation, and 'Sotto voce' in no-wake transcribes to the same spelling as the wake word.

userStories.title: Injected clock, turn assembler and pause detection (PRD US-005 part 1)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need raw transcription events turned into clean speaker-labeled turns, plus a reliable signal for when nobody is talking.
acceptanceCriteria: server/clock.ts provides a Clock interface (now(), setTimeout-like scheduling) with a real implementation and a simulated one for tests; all time-based server code uses an injected Clock, never Date.now() directly
Pure module server/asr/turns.ts consumes timestamped events and emits TurnUpdate (type in shared/): { turnId, speaker: string | null, text, final: boolean, startMs, endMs: number | null }
Partials replace (not append to) the current turn's text; a turn becomes final on speechComplete using that event's text
Speaker labels are attached per the behavior documented in fixtures/events/NOTES.md
Overlapping turns are tracked by turnId
Exposes pauseState(nowMs): { speaking: boolean, silentForMs: number }; speaking is true while any turn has speechStart without speechEnd
Unit tests replay every fixtures/events/*.jsonl file; for brainstorm: at least 2 distinct speakers, every final turn has non-empty text, final turns in time order, and at least one pause of >= 1.5 s
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Assembler is server/asr/turns.ts (TurnAssembler.accept(AsrFrameRecord) -> TurnUpdate | null, finalTurns(), openTurns(), pauseState(nowMs), malformedFrames()); types in shared/turns.ts; frame narrowing is asAsrEvent() in shared/asr.ts. SimulatedClock added to server/clock.ts. The >= 1.5 s pause criterion needed fixture work: brainstorm's longest scripted pause (1,600 ms) surfaced as only 1,084 ms, so line 18's pauseAfterMs went to 2,400 ms and the fixture was re-rendered and re-captured (gap now 1,944 ms). No line text, speaker or moment changed.

userStories.title: Transcription reconnect and speaker-label continuity (PRD US-005 part 2)
userStories.description: As a user, I want long sessions to keep going across the API's 60-minute session limit without losing who is who.
acceptanceCriteria: On close 1011 with reason 'Max session duration reached', the client opens a new realtime session and keeps streaming without dropping buffered audio
The assembler continues across sessions; new labels are mapped to existing speakers by order of first appearance, and a speakerMappingUncertain flag is set on subsequent TurnUpdates
Unit test with a mocked WebSocket server: forced 1011 mid-stream → reconnect → turns continue with mapped speakers and the flag set
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Max-session-duration (1011 + 'Max session duration reached') is handled separately from the retry path: immediate reconnect, no backoff, no retry budget spent. TurnAssembler maps a later session's labels onto known speakers by order of first appearance and flags those turns speakerMappingUncertain. Covered by unit tests against the local fake WebSocket server; no real capture is 60 minutes long, so the live path is untested against the API by design (see fixtures/events/NOTES.md).

userStories.title: Fast event replay with simulated time (PRD US-006)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want captured conversations to run through the pipeline in seconds without calling the transcription API, so interjection tuning is fast and cheap.
acceptanceCriteria: EventReplaySource feeds fixtures/events/<name>.jsonl into the turn assembler on a simulated Clock at a configurable speed ('1x' or 'max')
At 'max', idle time is skipped but simulated time does not advance past an in-flight async task registered with the clock (e.g. a model call) until it finishes
Unit test: replaying brainstorm events at 'max' produces the same final turns as at '1x' (run 1x on the simulated clock with real-time ratio check skipped)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: EventReplaySource in server/asr/EventReplaySource.ts; Clock.track/SimulatedClock.settle in server/clock.ts. 1x paces against an injected wallClock (systemClock by default), max spends no real time; both set the pipeline clock to each frame's recorded atMs, so the final turns are identical. The UI source selector for 'Replay events: <fixture>' is US-009's criterion, not this one.

userStories.title: Session folder persistence (PRD US-008)
userStories.description: As a user, I want every session saved so I can review it later, and so the build and evaluation can be checked by reading files.
acceptanceCriteria: SessionStore creates sessions/<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM>-<source>/ on session start
Writes session.json { id, startedAt, endedAt | null, source, speakers: { [label]: { name: string | null } }, asrSessions: string[], settings } on every change
Appends every raw transcription event to events.jsonl

Provides append/write methods (used by later stories) for board.md, board.json, candidates.jsonl, feedback.jsonl, answers.jsonl and artifacts/

Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Done; all 10 criteria met (npm run typecheck, npm test: 134 tests / 13 files, npm run test:integration, npm run fixtures:check). server/session/SessionStore.ts implements the SessionWriter interface - that interface is the list of which later story owns which file. Fixed on the way: the assembler was given startedAtMs = liveClock.now() on the live path while frame atMs is measured from the start of the stream, so transcript offsets (and pauseState's silence origin, which US-012 needs) were off by the process uptime. Both paths now start at 0. Nothing human-only is pending.

userStories.title: Board model, operations and markdown rendering (PRD US-009 part 1)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a board data model updated by small operations so items keep stable IDs and the board never churns.
acceptanceCriteria: Board type in shared/: { summary, constraints: Item[], points: Item[], questions: Item[], decisions: Item[] }, Item = { id, text, status: 'open'|'covered'|'dropped', sourceTurnIds: string[], createdAtMs, updatedAtMs }

BoardOp union: add_constraint | add_point | add_question | add_decision { text, sourceTurnIds }, set_status { id, status }, edit_text { id, text }, set_summary { text }; plus a JSON Schema for it usable as strict structured output
Pure applyOps(board, ops, nowMs) never deletes items (drop = status 'dropped'), ignores and reports unknown IDs, and assigns stable IDs (c1, p1, q1, d1…)
renderBoardMarkdown(board) produces board.md with sections Summary, Constraints, Points, Open Questions, Decisions using - [ ] / - [x] and ~~dropped~~
Unit tests cover every op, unknown IDs, and markdown output
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Done; all 7 criteria met (npm run typecheck, npm test: 188 tests / 19 files, npm run fixtures:check 9 OK). Types, zod schemas and the structured-output JSON Schema are in shared/board.ts; applyOps is server/board/applyOps.ts and renderBoardMarkdown is server/board/markdown.ts. boardOpsJsonSchema is hand-written rather than emitted by z.toJSONSchema, which produces oneOf and minItems/maxItems - keywords strict structured output rejects; shared/board.test.ts holds the hand-written schema and the zod union in agreement (same op kinds, same required fields, every object closed, no unsupported keywords), so edit both or the test fails. The schema has not yet been sent to the real API - US-014 is the first call, and if Meta rejects it the test's unsupportedKeywords list is where to record what else it dislikes. applyOps also returns changedIds and summaryChanged, which US-015's 3-second highlight needs, and length limits (12 words, 2 sentences) are prompt-side only: they are asked for in the schema descriptions and not enforced, because maxLength is not allowed.

userStories.title: Board update loop with Muse Spark (PRD US-009 part 2)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the discussion organized automatically into constraints, points, questions and decisions without anyone asking.
acceptanceCriteria: Update runs when >= 4 new final turns arrived or 45 s passed (on the injected Clock) with >= 1 new final turn; only one update in flight; triggers during flight merge into the next run

Each update calls muse-spark-1.3 (openai SDK, baseURL https://api.meta.ai/v1) with the board JSON, new final turns with turn IDs, and the 10 preceding turns; strict JSON-Schema output of BoardOp[]; response validated with zod

Prompt lives in server/prompts/board.md and instructs: items <= 12 words, prefer edit_text over duplicates, record every stated constraint, mark covered only when clearly addressed, summary <= 2 sentences
After each update: board.json and board.md written via SessionStore, and the board pushed over /ws/events

Integration test (events replay at max): brainstorm yields >= 4 points, >= 1 decision, >= 1 question, non-empty summary; moment-contradiction yields a constraint whose sourceTurnIds include a turn overlapping the planted setup line (use timing.json)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Done; all 7 criteria met (npm run typecheck, npm test: 215 tests / 21 files, npm run test:integration: 10 tests / 3 files, npm run fixtures:check: 9 OK, npm run build). Arrived on a dirty tree: a cut-off iteration had already written server/model/client.ts, server/prompts/, server/board/BoardUpdater.ts and the bus/SessionManager/useSessionEvents wiring, all of it typechecking and passing. This iteration added the missing integration test (server/board/board.integration.test.ts) and fixed npm run build. The model seam is ModelClient in server/model/client.ts (MuseClient is the real one); pass { completions } to keep a unit test offline. Prompts are server/prompts/*.md via loadPrompt(PROMPTS.<name>) - add a key to PROMPTS for a new one. BoardUpdater drives the model status dot (connecting around each call, active after), and SessionManager guards that on the session still being current. SessionManager now takes createModel so unit tests pass () => null; a session with no model still transcribes and still saves, it just has no board. The integration test cost ~110 s and ~13 real calls for both fixtures; it passed first try, no prompt tuning needed.

userStories.title: Observer: interjection candidates (PRD US-012)
userStories.description: As the system, I need to notice things worth raising (contradictions, factual errors, untested assumptions, dropped threads) and score them.
acceptanceCriteria: Observer runs right after each board update with the board, turns since its last run, and the last 3 final turns marked as current topic

Calls muse-spark-1.3 with strict structured output returning 0–3 candidates: { type, headline (<= 90 chars), detail (<= 60 words), whyNow (<= 20 words), evidenceTurnIds, relatedBoardItemIds, scores: { relevance, novelty, importance, confidence } } (each 0–1); validated with zod
Prompt in server/prompts/observer.md defines each type with one example and states that zero candidates is the normal result
Each candidate gets an ID and is appended to candidates.jsonl before any policy decision
Duplicates of earlier candidates (same type and overlapping relatedBoardItemIds) are marked duplicate and not passed on
Integration test (events replay at max): moment-contradiction produces >= 1 contradiction candidate whose evidenceTurnIds include a turn overlapping the trigger line
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Observer in server/interject/Observer.ts; candidate model, zod schema and the hand-written strict JSON Schema in shared/candidates.ts; prompt in server/prompts/observer.md. Wired in SessionManager.modelLoops(): the board and the observer share one ModelClient, and BoardUpdater.onUpdate calls observer.observe(board), so the look happens right after each update. The PRD's length limits are enforced by clipping inside the zod schema (strict structured output rejects maxLength/maximum), and scores are clamped to 0-1. Candidates are validated one at a time so a malformed one does not discard its neighbours. All 8 criteria met: npm run typecheck, npm test (282 tests / 26 files), npm run test:integration (14 tests / 4 files), npm run build. moment-contradiction produced exactly one candidate across the whole conversation - the planted contradiction, citing turn 0:20 (the trigger line) - and brainstorm produced none at all.

userStories.title: Fact verification with web search (PRD US-013)
userStories.description: As the system, before I tell a group they've got a fact wrong, I need to check it.
acceptanceCriteria: Every factual_error candidate is verified with a Responses API call (muse-spark-1.3, tools [{ type: 'web_search' }]) returning structured { verdict: 'wrong'|'right'|'unclear', correction (<= 30 words), citations: { url, title }[] }; citations taken from url_citation annotations (see https://dev.meta.ai/docs/cookbook/search-grounding)
wrong: candidate continues with correction appended to detail and citations attached; right/unclear: marked unverified in candidates.jsonl and stops
Verification runs asynchronously and does not block other candidates
Integration test (events replay at max): moment-fact yields a verified factual_error candidate with >= 1 citation
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Done; all 6 criteria met (npm run typecheck, npm test: 325 tests / 27 files, npm run test:integration: 18 tests / 5 files, npm run build). MuseClient.grounded is the Responses API seam (web_search + strict structured output + include: web_search_call.action.sources); Verifier runs checks concurrently and tracked on the clock; wrong continues with the correction in detail and citations attached, right/unclear/failed are logged unverified and stop. Two things had to change outside the verifier to make the criterion honest: (1) a Candidate now carries evidence quotes, because the observer's headline states the correction and sending it as the claim returned 'right' on a wrong conversation; (2) server/prompts/observer.md now tells the observer a checkable claim gets checked downstream, because it returned ZERO candidates for moment-fact across five looks otherwise - brainstorm still returns zero. FOUND, NOT FIXED (US-014's board loop): board update 6 of moment-fact fails with finish_reason 'length' at the 4096 default max_tokens once the board is ~15 items, and the retry fails the same way, so the last turns never reach the board. Raise the board call's maxTokens.

userStories.title: Interjection policy (PRD US-014)
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto to speak up rarely, at good moments, and only about things that matter.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure module server/interject/policy.ts decides silent | glow | interject | hold for a candidate given the Clock, pauseState and history
score = importance × confidence × (0.5 + 0.5 × relevance) × novelty
Chattiness thresholds (glow / interject): quiet 0.45 / 0.75, normal 0.35 / 0.6 (default), active 0.25 / 0.45
Timing: glow and interject only delivered during a pause (not speaking and silentForMs >= 1500); otherwise hold and re-check when pauseState changes
Expiry: held candidates become silent (reason stale) after 90 s or 6 new final turns
Budget: after an interject, further interjects downgrade to glow for 3 minutes; at most 3 interjects per 15 minutes
Courtesy: nothing delivered while an answer is thinking or within 5 s after a wake phrase is detected (expose hooks the answer and wake stories will call)
Every decision logged to candidates.jsonl with score, thresholds and reason (below_threshold, cooldown, budget, stale, courtesy, delivered)
Chattiness selectable live in the header and saved to session.json settings
Unit tests on a simulated clock cover threshold boundaries, hold→deliver on pause, expiry by time and by turns, cooldown downgrade, budget cap, courtesy suppression
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Pure rules in server/interject/policy.ts, the stateful half in InterjectionPolicy.ts. Decisions are a third kind in candidates.jsonl. Chattiness lives on the bus (snapshot is seven events now), is set by POST /api/session/settings and saved to session.json. Checked: typecheck, npm test (366), npm run test:integration (19), npm run build, and npm run verify:chattiness in a real browser.

userStories.title: Interjection delivery and feedback (PRD US-015)
userStories.description: As a user, I want Sotto's contributions shown calmly and clearly, and I want to tell it when it got the call wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: interject decisions render as interject cards with headline, why now, detail, evidence quotes and citations; glow decisions render as glow cards
Clicking an evidence quote scrolls the transcript to that turn and highlights it
Each delivered card has feedback buttons 👍 useful, 👎 not useful, ⏱ wrong moment; clicks append to feedback.jsonl with candidate ID and level
No sound and no modal on delivery
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using webapp-testing skill (Playwright screenshot after a moment-contradiction events replay shows an interject card)
userStories.notes: Done; all 6 criteria met. server/interject/delivery.ts is pure (Interjection -> StageCard: level becomes variant, quotes re-attributed to the names the group gave the labels, card id derived as card-<candidateId>). EventBus remembers cards and clears them on a session *starting*, so a finished replay keeps its stage and a reload is caught up; the snapshot is now seven events plus one `card` per card. POST /api/feedback takes only a card id (409 no-cards, 404 unknown-card, 400 bad body) and writes FeedbackLogRecord to the most recent session's feedback.jsonl. Clicking an evidence quote scrolls the transcript to that turn, marks it (data-cited) and stops following the live edge. Needed REPLAY_TRAILING_SILENCE_MS (3 s on the pipeline clock, after the board/observer/verifier flush and before the policy's last look): moment-contradiction has no reported silence >= 1,500 ms anywhere, so without it every candidate dies session_ended. Checked: npm run typecheck, npm test (383 / 30 files), npm run test:integration (19 / 5 files, 177 s), npm run build, and npm run verify:delivery - a real replay delivered the planted contradiction as an interject card 145 s after Start, the quote scrolled turn 0:20 into view, the verdict landed in feedback.jsonl, and 0 sounds / 0 dialogs were counted. Screenshots /tmp/sotto-shots/us020*.png. Nothing human-only is pending.

userStories.title: Eval runner and judge (PRD US-016 part 1)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to replay every evaluation fixture through the interjection engine and match delivered cards to planted moments.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run eval replays captured events at max speed for brainstorm, no-wake and every moment-* fixture through board → observer → verification → policy, at --chattiness quiet|normal|active|all (default normal)
Collects every delivered card with level, simulated delivery time, and whether delivery happened during a pause
Judge: muse-spark-1.3 strict structured output { matches: boolean, reason } for each (delivered card, moment in that fixture) pair; prompt in server/prompts/judge.md
Judge results cached on disk in eval/cache/ keyed by hash of (card headline + detail, moment id, judge prompt hash) so reruns are cheap
Raw run results written to eval/runs/<timestamp>.json
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Done; all 7 criteria met (npm run typecheck, npm test: 431 / 36 files, npm run build, and a real `npm run eval` over the whole set). Code is server/eval/ (runner, judge + disk cache, pause reconstruction, moment resolution, arg parsing) with the CLI at scripts/eval.ts and the types in shared/eval.ts; eval/runs, eval/cache and eval/sessions are git-ignored (eval/README.md documents the layout). The runner starts an ordinary SessionManager session at replaySpeed 'max' and reads deliveries off the event bus's card events, so there is no second pipeline; 'during a pause' is reconstructed from the turns (server/eval/pause.ts, held against TurnAssembler.pauseState in a test) and passed through the policy's own inPause(). Real run 2026-10-28_091323, 7 fixtures at chattiness normal, 700 s wall clock: 1 card delivered, 0 outside a pause, 1 judge call (matched). US-022 should read the run file rather than re-replaying. Recall is the thing US-023 has to fix, and the run file already says why: brainstorm and no-wake produce zero candidates (good), but of the five moment fixtures only moment-contradiction delivered - moment-assumption and moment-dropped produced no candidate at all, while moment-fact's verified-wrong Instagram claim and both of moment-mixed's candidates went silent/stale on turnsWaited >= STALE_TURNS (6) because those captures have almost no reported silence >= 1,500 ms.

userStories.title: Eval scoring, report and gates (PRD US-016 part 2)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want clear numbers on how well Sotto chooses what to raise and when.
acceptanceCriteria: Per moment outcome: caught (matched, expected level or higher, within window: after triggerLine ends and before deadlineLine ends per timing.json), caught_low (glow when interject expected), late (after deadline), missed
Per fixture: false interjects (interject cards matching no moment) and false glows
Timing: percent of deliveries during a pause (must be 100%) and median delay from triggerLine end to delivery
Headline metrics: moment recall = (caught + caught_low) / total; interject precision = true interjects / all interjects; false interjects on brainstorm + no-wake
Writes eval/reports/<timestamp>.md with per-moment table, totals, settings, git commit, prompt file hashes and estimated API cost; prints a terminal table
Exits non-zero if recall < 0.7, any false interject on brainstorm or no-wake, or any delivery outside a pause
Scoring logic is a pure function with unit tests using hand-built run results
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Tune interjections to targets
userStories.description: As the team, we want the interjection engine to meet its targets before building the remaining features.
acceptanceCriteria: Run npm run eval at normal chattiness; iterate on server/prompts/observer.md (and, only if needed, policy weights) until recall >= 0.7, zero false interjects on brainstorm and no-wake, and 100% deliveries during pauses
Do NOT edit fixtures, moment annotations, the judge prompt, or the scoring code to reach targets
Spot-check at least 5 judge decisions by reading the cards and moments; record agreement in the report notes
Commit the passing report in eval/reports/ and summarize what changed in progress.txt
If targets are not reached after 5 eval iterations, commit the best report, leave passes false, and write the gap and hypotheses in notes
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Wake-phrase detection (PRD US-017)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to address Sotto by name mid-conversation and have it know I'm asking it something.
acceptanceCriteria: Pure module server/wake.ts: detect(text) → { triggered, question | null }

Triggers when the wake word starts a sentence or follows hey/okay/ok, followed by a comma or a question; spellings configurable, default ['sotto', 'soto', 'sota'] plus any spellings recorded in fixtures/events/NOTES.md
Does not trigger on 'so to speak', 'so to', 'sotto voce', or 'Soto' as a name inside a sentence ('Soto's restaurant')
Unit tests: >= 8 positive and >= 8 negative sentences, including the no-wake look-alikes
Partial turn trigger shows a 'Sotto is listening…' indicator in the UI and calls the policy courtesy hook; the question is emitted only when the turn is final; at most one trigger per turnId
Integration test (events replay at max): ask-search gives exactly 1 trigger; no-wake, brainstorm and all moment-* give 0
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Answer agent with web search (PRD US-018)
userStories.description: As a user, I want a short, sourced answer that uses the conversation as context.
acceptanceCriteria: On a wake question, calls the Responses API (muse-spark-1.3, tools [{ type: 'web_search' }], streaming) with the board, the last 10 minutes of final turns with speaker names, and the question; prompt in server/prompts/answer.md
Prompt: line 1 is a headline <= 90 chars for people glancing at a shared screen, then optional markdown detail <= 150 words

Parses into Answer { id, question, askedBy, headline, detailMd, citations: { url, title }[], status: thinking|done|error, createdAtMs, latencyMs }; citations from url_citation annotations, deduped by URL
Streams as an answer card: thinking immediately, headline as soon as line 1 completes, full answer when done; calls the policy courtesy hook while thinking
Answers run in their own queue and never wait for board or observer
API errors produce status error with a short message; session continues
Each answer appended to answers.jsonl
Integration test (events replay at max): ask-search gives 1 answer with status done, headline <= 90 chars, >= 1 citation
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using webapp-testing skill (Playwright screenshot after ask-search events replay shows the answer card)

userStories.title: Typed questions (PRD US-019)

acceptanceCriteria: 'Ask Sotto…' input at the bottom of the stage; Enter submits
Typed questions use the same path as spoken ones with askedBy 'typed'
Works during a session and after Stop (using the last session's context)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: HTML artifacts on the stage (PRD US-020)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to ask for a diagram, table or mockup and see it rendered.
acceptanceCriteria: Answer agent can call function tool show_html({ title, html }) where html is a complete self-contained document (inline CSS/JS/SVG, no external requests)
Server saves to artifacts/<nn>-<slug>.html and attaches { title, path } to the answer

Card renders it in <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> (no allow-same-origin) served from /api/sessions/<id>/artifacts/<file> with header Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:
Artifact card has an 'open full screen' button

If the API rejects web_search combined with function tools in one request, route by intent: a cheap classification call picks 'search' or 'visual' and the matching tool set; record the approach used in fixtures/events/NOTES.md
Integration test (events replay at max): ask-diagram gives an answer with exactly 1 artifact whose file exists and contains <svg or <div
Tests pass

Prints per-fixture latency: wake → headline, wake → done, moment trigger → delivery
